## Proof

Let $H = 1 - \tfrac12 + \tfrac13 - \cdots + \tfrac1{1319} = \sum_{k=1}^{1319}\frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k}$, and let $a/b = H$ in lowest terms.

**Step 1 — Rewrite as a harmonic difference.** Since $1319 = 2\cdot 660 - 1$, set $n = 660$. Splitting odd/even indices,
$$H = \sum_{j=1}^{n}\frac1{2j-1} - \sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\frac1{2j} = \Bigl(H_{2n-1} - \tfrac12 H_{n-1}\Bigr) - \tfrac12 H_{n-1} = H_{2n-1} - H_{n-1}.$$
Hence
$$H = \sum_{k=n}^{2n-1}\frac1k = \sum_{k=660}^{1319}\frac1k.$$

**Step 2 — Set up the modular computation.** Let $p = 1979$ (prime). Since $p > 1319$, every $k\in[660,1319]$ is invertible in $\mathbb F_p$. The denominator $b\mid\operatorname{lcm}(660,\dots,1319)$, so all prime factors of $b$ are $\le 1319 < p$; thus $\gcd(b,p)=1$ and $b$ is invertible mod $p$. Consequently
$$a \equiv b\cdot H \pmod p.$$

**Step 3 — Show $H\equiv 0\pmod p$.** In $\mathbb F_p$,
$$H \equiv \sum_{k=660}^{1319} k^{-1} \pmod p.$$
The key observation is $p = 1979 = 660 + 1319$, so the set $S=\{660,\dots,1319\}$ is invariant under $k\mapsto p-k$ (since $p-660=1319$ and $p-1319=660$). Therefore
$$\sum_{k\in S}k^{-1} \equiv \sum_{k\in S}(p-k)^{-1}\equiv \sum_{k\in S}(-k)^{-1} = -\sum_{k\in S}k^{-1}\pmod p.$$
So $2H\equiv 0\pmod p$. Since $p=1979$ is odd, $2$ is invertible, giving $H\equiv 0\pmod p$.

**Step 4 — Conclude.** From Step 2,
$$a \equiv b\cdot H \equiv b\cdot 0 \equiv 0 \pmod{1979}.$$

The remainder when $a$ is divided by $1979$ is $\boxed{0}$.
